newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa set to step up gasoline imports.
newsitem.headline: South Africa set to step up gasoline imports.

text.p: After years of almost total self-reliance, South Africa is set to become a net importer of gasoline over the next year, industry sources said on Monday.
"From 1997 onwards, petrol production will be at the limit of capacity," South African Petroleum Industry Association director Colin McClelland told Reuters.
South Africa was expected to produce 12.26 billion litres of gasoline this year while demand was expected to be 11.37 billion litres.

The first few imports have already taken place this year because of several refinery shutdowns, with reports of 500,000 barrels of gasoline shipped from Singapore to South Africa and neighbouring countries in September.
Traders were coy as to where they would source future supplies of gasoline. On said simply "We'll buy where it's cheapest."
Increased imports would have no impact on domestic prices because these are set in terms of a formula based on Singapore and Bahrain prices.
Sources said oil companies would be reluctant to expand capacity in any major way until there was greater certainty about future government policies and refining margins improved.
Several South African businesses, including leading retailer Pick 'n Pay, have been lobbying government for some time to deregulate the oil industry so that they could import gasoline.
Pick 'n Pay chairman Raymond Ackerman claimed that he would be able to import very competitively priced gasoline.
But South Africa would remain a net exporter of diesel until after 2000, industry sources said.
Total production this year was expected to be 8.92 billion litres agaianst expected consumption of 6.3 billion litres.
